relevance_reason: The paper reports a homozygous nonsense BORCS5 variant in two sibs with neuroaxonal dystrophy and osteopetrosis, agenesis of the corpus callosum and ventriculomegaly. This bears directly on a BORCS5-related neurodegeneration entry.

findings.statement: Fisher et al. (2025) reported 2 sibs born to consanguineous Pakistani parents. Prenatal imaging showed cerebral ventriculomegaly and agenesis of the corpus callosum in both. Autopsies on both sibs showed similar abnormalities, including facial dysmorphism, osteopetrosis, and neuropathologic findings consistent with neuroaxonal dystrophy.
quotes: We report on sibs, born to consanguineous Pakistani parents identified prenatally with cerebral ventriculomegaly and agenesis of the corpus callosum, and autopsies done on both showed similar abnormalities, including facial dysmorphism, osteopetrosis, and neuropathologic findings consistent with NAD.

findings.statement: In 2 sibs, born to consanguineous Pakistani parents, who had neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis, Fisher et al. (2025) used trio exome sequencing to identify a homozygous nonsense variant in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene (c.283C>T, p.Arg95Ter; NM_058169.4). Each parent was heterozygous for the variant.
quotes: Trio exome sequencing identified a homozygous c.283 C>T; p.(Arg95Ter) variant in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene (NM_058169.4) in each of the couple's fetuses, and each of the parents was heterozygous for this variant.

findings.statement: Fisher et al. (2025) found that 1 of the 2 affected sibs was also homozygous for a missense variant of uncertain significance in the SCYL2 gene (c.902G>A, p.Arg301His; NM_017988.5), for which both parents were heterozygous. Because the autopsy findings in the 2 sibs were identical, the authors raised the possibility that the SCYL2 variant did not contribute to the phenotype.
quotes: one of the affected fetuses was also homozygous for a biallelic missense VUS variant in SCYL2 (NM_017988.5) c.902G>A; p. Arg301His, heterozygous in parents.
the autopsy findings on the two sibs were identical, raising the possibility that this SCYL2 homozygote variant did not contribute to the phenotype.

findings.statement: Fisher et al. (2025) noted that neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis was first reported in a consanguineous Moroccan Jewish family and that, until their report, no genetic variant had been linked to the disease.
quotes: Neuroaxonal dystrophy (NAD) with osteopetrosis syndrome (OMIM # 600329) was first reported in a consanguineous Moroccan Jewish family. However, to date, no genetic variant has been linked to this disease.

relevance_reason: Exome sequencing study of 31 mostly consanguineous Arab families with neurologic disease. It lists AAR2 among novel candidate disease genes, but the variant and clinical details are only in supplementary tables that were not supplied, so the paper provides only limited context for this entry.

findings.statement: Charng et al. (2016) performed whole-exome sequencing in 31 mostly consanguineous Arab families from Saudi Arabia with neurologic disease, including brain malformations and/or developmental delay/intellectual disability. They proposed 12 novel candidate disease genes, including AAR2, in 11 families. Most variants in candidate genes mapped to regions of absence of heterozygosity and were homozygous. All variants in novel candidate genes were classified as variants of uncertain significance.
quotes: we propose and provide evidenced-based ranking for 12 novel candidate disease genes (GRM7, FOXP4, KIF5B, KDM2B, MLLT1, RPS6KC1, CDK20, MAGED2, TMEM47, AAR2, LOH12CR1, RSRC2) in 11 families
Most of the variants in potential candidate disease genes that we identified map to the AOH regions and are thus homozygous recessive.
This genomics study includes 31 Arab families exhibiting neurological disease phenotypes, among which 28 were reported to be consanguineous or from the same tribe
